lung histopathology.title: Various antibody clones of Napsin A, TTF-1, and p40 in non-small cell lung carcinoma
lung histopathology.text: This tissue-microarray study evaluated CK5, p63, and p40 as squamous markers and Napsin A and TTF-1 as lung adenocarcinoma markers. Reported performance varied by marker and antibody clone, and combining Napsin A with TTF-1 improved sensitivity.

lung histopathology.title: Immunostaining for TTF-1, Napsin A, p40, and cytokeratin 5 aids differential diagnosis of NSCLC
lung histopathology.text: The study compared marker combinations for separating lung adenocarcinoma from squamous cell carcinoma. TTF-1 and Napsin A supported adenocarcinoma, while p40 and CK5 supported squamous differentiation; the combined panel was more informative than a single stain.

lung histopathology.title: Value of napsin A and thyroid transcription factor-1 in the identification of primary lung adenocarcinoma
lung histopathology.text: In a cohort containing primary lung cancers and metastases, Napsin A and TTF-1 were frequently expressed in primary lung adenocarcinoma. The study also observed TTF-1 expression outside lung adenocarcinoma, supporting interpretation as a panel rather than as an isolated marker.

lung histopathology.title: Colorectal carcinoma: pathologic aspects
lung histopathology.text: Colorectal adenocarcinoma commonly forms malignant glands. Invasion can be accompanied by desmoplastic stroma, and glandular lumina frequently contain characteristic dirty necrosis. Benign colonic mucosa retains orderly crypt architecture and mature goblet cells without dysplasia.

lung histopathology.title: Sampling and confirmation in infectious esophagitis
lung histopathology.text: For suspected HSV esophagitis, diagnostic cytopathic changes are most likely at the ulcer edge and in sloughed squamous cells. Candida requires demonstration of pseudohyphae or true hyphae and assessment of tissue invasion rather than isolated budding yeasts in exudate. Histology may require organism-specific immunostaining, in situ hybridization, culture, or special stains for confirmation.

lung histopathology.title: Pulmonary adenocarcinoma histology
lung histopathology.text: Pulmonary adenocarcinoma can show lepidic, acinar, papillary, micropapillary, or solid growth with mucin, and mixed patterns are common. Squamous differentiation is supported morphologically by keratinization, keratin pearl formation, and intercellular bridges. Poorly differentiated tumors may require immunohistochemistry.

colon histopathology.title: Colorectal carcinoma: pathologic aspects

Benign colonic mucosa retains orderly crypt architecture and mature goblet cells without dysplasia.

colon histopathology.title: Decision tree for pulmonary adenocarcinoma with mucinous features versus metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma
colon histopathology.text: A decision tree using TTF-1, SATB2, CDX2, and CK7 was developed to distinguish primary pulmonary adenocarcinoma with mucinous features from metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma. The validation results support using multiple markers and clinical context when assigning a primary site.

colon histopathology.title: HNF4-alpha and SATB2 in pulmonary and colorectal adenocarcinomas
colon histopathology.text: In a large immunohistochemical series, Napsin A and TTF-1 were much more frequent in pulmonary adenocarcinoma, whereas CDX2, CK20, HNF4-alpha, and SATB2 were much more frequent in colorectal metastases. Rare cross-expression occurred, so no individual marker was absolute.

infectious esophagitis.title: Histologic features of herpes simplex virus esophagitis
infectious esophagitis.text: HSV esophagitis can show ulceration, necrotic debris, multinucleated giant squamous cells, ground-glass or eosinophilic intranuclear inclusions, nuclear molding, and chromatin margination. Viral immunohistochemistry or another confirmatory method may be needed because viral esophagitis patterns can overlap.

infectious esophagitis.title: Histologic features of Candida esophagitis
infectious esophagitis.text: Candida esophagitis shows fungal hyphae, pseudohyphae, and spores along or invading squamous epithelium, often with neutrophilic inflammation, erosion, ulceration, and necrotic debris. PAS or Grocott methenamine silver stains help demonstrate fungal forms and distinguish Candida from viral esophagitis.

infectious esophagitis.title: Histologic features of cytomegalovirus esophagitis
infectious esophagitis.text: CMV cytopathic effect is typically found in endothelial and stromal cells at the ulcer base. Histology may show cytomegaly, eccentrically positioned basophilic intranuclear inclusions surrounded by a clear halo, pale perinuclear regions, and an owl-eye appearance; CMV immunohistochemistry can confirm infected cells.
